They have modest efficacy, significant toxicity, and are best used when specific epigenetic abnormalities are documented.
faq.q: Why are epigenetic drugs not first‑line for most cancers?

faq.a: Deficiencies in folate, B12, and methionine reduce methyl donor availability, leading to global hypomethylation.

exam: A 45‑year‑old with AML shows poor response to standard chemotherapy – what epigenetic test would you order and why? — Test DNA methylation of tumor suppressor promoters; positive hypermethylation supports adding azacitidine.
A patient on azacitidine develops fever and neutropenia – what is your next step? — Stop drug, start broad‑spectrum antibiotics, and assess marrow recovery; infection risk is heightened.

Explain how chronic malaria infection could alter epigenetic regulation of immune genes. — Repeated antigen exposure induces histone modifications that dampen cytokine transcription, affecting immunity.
You have no access to methylation sequencing; how can you still assess epigenetic involvement in a suspected cancer? — Use immunohistochemistry for silenced proteins (e.g., p16) as surrogate markers.
Why might a child with sickle‑cell disease have variable severity despite identical genotype? — Epigenetic modifiers (DNA methylation, miRNA) influence fetal hemoglobin expression.
What are the contraindications for HDAC inhibitors in low‑resource settings? — Active hepatitis, severe liver disease, and lack of monitoring capacity for cytopenias.
Describe how folate supplementation could modify disease risk via epigenetics. — Provides methyl groups for DNMTs, maintaining normal promoter methylation and reducing oncogene activation.

Differentiate between a genetic mutation and epigenetic silencing of the same gene in a tumour. — Mutation changes the DNA code; silencing leaves the sequence intact but blocks transcription, often reversible.
ai.title: Epigenetics in Clinical Medicine
ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Epigenetics describes reversible DNA and histone modifications that regulate gene expression without changing the sequence. Clinicians must recognise how these changes influence disease risk, presentation, and treatment, especially in low‑resource settings.

b: Key mechanisms: DNA methylation, histone acetylation/methylation, micro‑RNA silencing
Changes are reversible, offering therapeutic targets
sections.p: Epigenetic mechanisms act like switches that turn genes on or off. They are shaped by environment, infections, nutrition, and drugs, and can be inherited across cell divisions.

b: DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs) add methyl groups
Histone acetyltransferases (HATs) and deacetylases (HDACs) modify histones
miRNA biogenesis occurs in nucleus → cytoplasm
sections.p: Methyl groups added to CpG islands silence transcription. Histone acetylation relaxes chromatin, promoting transcription; deacetylation condenses chromatin, repressing genes. Micro‑RNAs bind mRNA, preventing translation.

b: Nutrient‑derived methyl donors (folate, B12) affect methylation
Chronic infections can cause hypomethylation of inflammatory genes
sections.p: Environmental exposures (e.g., malaria, HIV, malnutrition) alter epigenetic marks, influencing immune response and disease susceptibility. Some drugs (e.g., azacitidine) deliberately modify epigenetics.

b: Hypermethylation of tumor‑suppressor genes → cancer
Global hypomethylation → genomic instability
Epigenetic dysregulation in sickle‑cell disease severity
sections.p: Aberrant epigenetic patterns contribute to cancer, congenital disorders, and metabolic disease. In low‑resource settings, infections and herbal remedies are common triggers.

b: Predicts response to hypomethylating agents in AML
Explains why some HIV patients progress faster despite similar viral loads
Guides counseling on reversible risk factors (smoking, diet)
sections.p: Understanding epigenetics helps explain variable disease phenotypes, guide drug choice, and anticipate treatment resistance, especially where diagnostic tools are limited.

t.b: Does the tumor have hypermethylated promoter of p16? → Positive suggests epigenetic silencing, may influence therapy
Is acetyl‑H3 increased after HDAC inhibitor? → Confirms drug target engagement
Are oncogenic miRNAs elevated? → Supports epigenetic contribution to malignancy

b: Use hypomethylating agents (azacitidine, decitabine) for myelodysplastic syndromes; avoid in severe infection due to marrow suppression
HDAC inhibitors (vorinostat) for cutaneous T‑cell lymphoma; monitor liver function
Optimize nutrition (folate, B12) to support normal methylation
Counsel on avoiding herbal toxins that may alter epigenetic enzymes
sections.p: Treat underlying cause, then consider epigenetic‑targeted therapy when indicated.

b: Mutations alter DNA sequence; epigenetics alters expression without sequence change
Both can coexist, e.g., mutated oncogene with promoter hypermethylation
Peripheral blood may not reflect tumor epigenetics
Acute infection can transiently change miRNA levels
sections.p: Normal methylation levels do not rule out disease; tissue‑specific patterns may be missed if blood is used.

b: Link environmental exposure to epigenetic change
Name a drug that reverses DNA methylation
Explain why epigenetic therapy may be contraindicated in active infection
sections.p: Focus on mechanisms, clinical impact, and how to work around limited tests.

whenToSeekHelp: Rapidly worsening cytopenias after hypomethylating therapy
Severe hepatic dysfunction with HDAC inhibitors
Unexplained neurological decline in a patient on epigenetic drugs
